item.title: International Business Got More Concrete When I Picked a Product
item.description: I used to think of international business as a broad thing: companies in different countries, distributors, prices, rules, and people trying to sell across borders. That list is true, but it is so broad that it is hard to learn much from it. For a small exercise, I worked with a specific product-market pair: Tunisian olive oil and Singapore. I used an AI assistant to help me find public data and organise the questions. I wanted to see what could be learned before talking to an importer or pretending to make a business recommendation. item.title: Persuasion Isn't Negotiation
item.description: I keep coming back to a basic difference: changing someone's mind is not the same job as agreeing what to do next. Imagine a contractor and a client arguing over a Friday deadline. The client keeps saying the date was promised; the contractor keeps explaining why the remaining work needs another day. They are trying to win different versions of the same argument. But the decision in front of them might be narrower: what can be delivered on Friday, what moves to Monday, and whether the changed schedule affects the price.
